note: Which per-view observation channel may be written into which training-package view.
The exporter reads this file (or SYNLAB_VIEW_CHANNEL_POLICY) and records the resolved
policy, its source and its hash in export_manifest.json; nothing in this list is a
hardcoded literal in synlab/storage/export.py.  Membership is a *permission*, not a claim:
what a package really contains is measured by scanning the written files, and a channel that
is permitted but absent is reported as missing.

channels.reason: pixels a deployment profile may obtain; a real acquisition knows its own usable mask
commanded slide position of the delivered view (rig metadata, not an answer)
camera z of the delivered view; a real rig with a depth sensor or MVS output provides it
channels.caveat: on this checkout depth comes from the renderer (`renderer depth is in mm by construction`); the field is the documented rig output, its values are simulated

channels.reason: the deployment mask channel itself, kept beside the RGB so a consumer need not infer it
pixels that cannot be attributed to one surface (mixture / defocus / depth edge); an acquisition can estimate this
channels.caveat: on a real rig this channel is an estimate, not the renderer's exact mixed-pixel labelling

channels.reason: the working region of interest; acquisition-side (which part of the frame the operator targeted)
camera intrinsics: a real acquisition is given fx/fy/cx/cy by calibration (p1163)
channels.caveat: the three camera profiles of configs/a12/camera_profiles.json are all calibrated=false / STRESS_UNCALIBRATED, so the shipped K is a declared profile, not a measured calibration

channels.reason: scene-linear radiance before the ISP: a training-time analysis channel, not a delivered product
per-face integer label: it names the answer surface of every pixel
face attribute tag map: it separates original wall from new fracture surface
the ground-truth camera pose of the view
the exact distortion coefficients the renderer applied (a calibration target, not an input)

note: Roles whose payload is a ground-truth layer.  Their channel sets are never copied into the
deployment view: clean/physical/visible truth and the iface_*/corr_* correspondence arrays
stay on the research side, where the layered label tables consume them.
